title: Terp Standard - a release's resolved deployment
description: What one release runs, resolved and closed: the document a release tool writes into the signed release manifest, and that an executor runs instead of reading the app's Compose files. It holds what the release decides: its services, their images by digest, their commands, the references their variables resolve from, their mounts, probes and start order. It holds nothing an executor or an environment owns: the restart policy, networks, published ports, labels, logging, container hardening, resources and instance counts. A field that does not apply is absent, never null, and a reader refuses a field it does not know, at any depth.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this vocabulary. A reader refuses a version it does not carry rather than read a later document with an earlier vocabulary.

services.description: One service per unit of the release's deployment declaration, in the declaration's order: no more and no fewer, each id once.

items.description: One service: the declared unit it realises, and everything an executor needs to run it.

role.description: The declared unit's role, carried as information: an executor decides nothing on it and acts only on the closed fields beside it.

lifecycle.description: Whether the service runs until it is stopped, or runs to completion. It decides the restart policy the executor writes, which this document never states.

datastore.description: Present for a unit that runs a datastore: its kind and version, which the release's datastore table must hold.

kind.description: The datastore's kind, as the declaration names it.

version.description: The datastore's version, as the declaration names it.

image.description: The image the service runs, by repository and sha256 digest, never a tag. A built image is one of the release's built images; a datastore's is the datastore table's reference for its kind and version.

command.description: The argv the service runs, one argument per string: never one string a reader would have to split. Absent: the image's own command. Absent on the migration service, whose argv the executor owns.

init.description: Whether the executor runs an init process as the service's first process, so signals reach the app and exited children are reaped.

environment.description: The variables the release sets for the service, in ascending order of name, each name once. A value is a literal, or a reference the executor resolves from the environment it deploys to.

items.description: One variable: its name, and where its value comes from.

name.description: The variable's name. A name the executor owns is refused (refusedEnvironmentNames, refusedEnvironmentPrefixes).

source.description: Where the value comes from. 'value': the literal beside it. 'config': the deployed environment's configuration, under 'key'. 'secret': the deployed environment's secrets, under 'key'. 'database': the connection the executor gives the app's runtime role; its 'key' is always 'runtime', because the connection that may change the schema never reaches a service.

value.description: The literal value, for source 'value'. It is the value itself: no reader expands anything in it.

key.description: The configuration or secret name the executor resolves, or 'runtime' for source 'database'.

appEnvironment.description: Whether the executor also gives the service the variables the app declares for the environment it deploys to, from that environment's configuration and secrets.

mounts.description: The service's mounts, in ascending order of target, each target once.

items.description: One mount: a named volume of the release, or an anonymous volume over a path the image declares and no other mount covers.

type.description: 'volume': a named volume listed in 'volumes'. 'anonymous': a volume with no name, which no backup covers. Version 1 carries no bind mount.

target.description: Where the mount sits in the container: an absolute path with no empty, '.' or '..' segment. It is never the app root /srv or a path under it, except the files storage root /srv/var/files: a volume over code would keep that code across releases.

readOnly.description: Whether the service may only read the volume, for type 'volume'.

serves.description: Present for a service that answers HTTP: the port inside the container, and the path that tells whether it is healthy. Whether and where the port is published is the executor's choice.

port.description: The port the service listens on inside the container.

healthPath.description: The path an executor reads to judge the service healthy, as the declaration resolves it for the unit's role.

healthcheck.description: The service's container health probe and its timing, in whole seconds.

form.description: 'exec': an argv run without a shell. 'shell': a script run by the image's /bin/sh -c, so the image must carry a shell.

retries.description: Consecutive failures that make the service unhealthy.

startPeriodSeconds.description: Seconds after the service starts during which a failed probe does not count.

after.description: The services this one starts after, in ascending order of unit, each unit once, with the condition it waits for.

items.description: One service this one starts after, and the condition it waits for.

unit.description: A service of this document, never the service itself.

condition.description: 'started': the unit's container runs. 'healthy': its health probe passes, so it must have one. 'completed': it ran to completion and succeeded, so it must be one-shot.

volumes.description: The named volumes the services mount, in ascending order: every name a volume mount uses, and no other.

migration.description: The one-shot service the executor runs the migration step in, with an argv the executor owns and the connection that may change the schema. Absent: the release has no such service, and the executor runs the step in an api service's image.

refusedEnvironmentNames.description: Variable names a release never sets. The executor owns them, and sets from its own host's configuration what a host needs, such as a proxy or a certificate bundle.

refusedEnvironmentPrefixes.description: Prefixes of variable names a release never sets: each changes how the interpreter, the dynamic loader, the container tooling or certificate checking behaves.
